mainTopic: Finding several buried bodies: when they count as a שכונת קברות (a graveyard), how far one must keep checking, and whose opinion about the size of a burial cave the source follows
overview: The amud continues a source about someone who digs and finds buried bodies. If he finds three bodies four to eight אמות apart, the place is a real graveyard: he may not move them, and he must keep searching twenty more אמות. Even one more body found there extends the search another twenty. The גמרא asks whose opinion the four-to-eight measurement follows, since the רבנן say a burial chamber is four by six and רבי שמעון says six by eight. It answers with a ברייתא showing another version of רבי שמעון that does use four to eight. Then it challenges this from the twenty-אמות search: by רבי שמעון it should be twenty-two, and by the רבנן eighteen. It answers that this line follows the רבנן, where one chamber was searched along its longer diagonal. Asked why the second chamber isn't measured diagonally too, the גמרא answers that we assume one diagonal, not two.

steps.title: Three bodies found: it is a graveyard
steps.stepSummary: The source rules that if one finds three bodies with four to eight אמות between them, the place is a שכונת קברות, and he must check twenty אמות further.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found three bodies, and the distance between them is from four to eight אמות, this is a graveyard. He must check from there onward for twenty אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its quote of a source about finding buried bodies. Three bodies spaced four to eight אמות apart are treated as a real graveyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single body found by surprise may be moved. But three bodies laid out at the distances of a normal burial chamber show this is a planned burial site. So the bodies stay, and he must search further for more graves.

keyTerms.meaning: A graveyard; an established burial area whose graves may not be moved
A cubit, a unit of length (about half a meter)

phrases.english: If he found three bodies

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בֵּינֵיהֶן מֵאַרְבַּע עַד שְׁמוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: if there is between them from four to eight cubits,
phrases.notes: "Between them" means the distance from the first body to the last one.

phrases.english: this is a graveyard,
and he checks from it onward twenty cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source the גמרא was already quoting on the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three bodies spaced four to eight אמות apart make a שכונת קברות, and one must search twenty more אמות.

steps.title: Finding another body keeps the search going
steps.stepSummary: If one more body turns up at the end of the twenty אמות, he must search another twenty, because there is good reason to expect more graves. Had he found that body alone at first, he could have moved it with its surrounding earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found one body at the end of the twenty אמות, he checks from it onward another twenty אמות, because there is a basis for the matter. Had he found it at first, by itself, he would take it and its surrounding earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The source continues: once you know you are in a graveyard, even one more body means you must keep searching another twenty אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One lone body normally proves nothing, and it may be moved together with its תפוסה (the earth around it). But here the earlier discovery already shows this is a graveyard. So even one more body is a sign that the graveyard keeps going.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a basis or strong sign for the matter (literally, 'the matter has legs')
Its surrounding earth, which is taken along when a body is moved

steps.whatToRemember: Context changes everything. A single body on its own may be moved, but a single body inside a known graveyard is another sign of the graveyard and extends the search.

phrases.english: If he found one at the end of twenty cubits
he checks from it onward twenty cubits,
for there is a basis for the matter.
Even though, had he found it at first,
he would take it and its surrounding earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same source, extending the search rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One more body found within the search area extends the search another twenty אמות, even though a lone body found at first could be moved.

steps.title: Whose opinion is four to eight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who holds that a burial chamber measures four to eight אמות. The רבנן say four by six, and רבי שמעון says six by eight, so neither seems to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'from four to eight.' Whose opinion is this? If it is the רבנן, don't they say four אמות by six? If it is רבי שמעון, doesn't he say six by eight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts analyzing the source and asks whose opinion the four-to-eight measurement follows. Neither known opinion fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-to-eight distance assumes a burial chamber is four by eight. But earlier (on 100b) the רבנן said four by six, and רבי שמעון said six by eight. So the source seems to match no one, and that is a real challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said'; the גמרא's way of quoting a line it is about to discuss

phrases.english: The Master said:
From four to eight.
Whose opinion is this?
If it is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרִי: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַל שֵׁשׁ!
phrases.english: don't they say: four cubits by six!
phrases.notes: This is their measurement for a burial chamber, from the earlier משנה on 100b.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Shimon,
doesn't he say: six by eight!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מֵאַרְבַּע וְעַד שְׁמוֹנֶה. מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the quoted source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The four-to-eight measurement in the source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither the רבנן (four by six) nor רבי שמעון (six by eight) holds that a burial chamber is four by eight, so the source has no known author.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, in another version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source really follows רבי שמעון, as reported by a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is רבי שמעון, and it is this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the source does follow רבי שמעון, but in the version reported by another תנא. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not change the source. It says a different report of רבי שמעון's view exists, and that report uses four to eight. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Actually'; used to keep an original assumption while defending it
And it is this particular תנא (who reports the opinion differently)

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Shimon,
and it is this tanna,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different version of a known opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי שמעון only holds six by eight, so the source matches no one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another תנא reports רבי שמעון as using four to eight, so the source follows that version.

steps.title: The ברייתא with רבי שמעון's four to eight
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי שמעון בן יהודה quoting רבי שמעון: when bodies lie close together, ignore the middle ones, and the outer ones combine at four to eight אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If he found them lying close together, without four to eight אמות between them, they have תפוסה but are not a graveyard. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: We view the middle ones as if they are not there, and the rest combine at four to eight אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves this other version of רבי שמעון. Here רבי שמעון does use the four-to-eight measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view says bodies packed tightly together are not a real graveyard, since real graves aren't placed that close, so they can be moved with their earth. רבי שמעון, as reported by רבי שמעון בן יהודה, ignores the middle bodies and measures the outer ones. If they are four to eight apart, it is a graveyard. This shows a version of רבי שמעון that uses four to eight.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught in a ברייתא
Lying close together, one right after another

phrases.english: As it was taught: If he found them lying close together,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּינֵיהֶן מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַד שְׁמוֹנֶה –
phrases.english: and there is not four to eight cubits between them,
they have surrounding earth,
but they do not have the status of a graveyard.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
We view the middle ones as if they are not there,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְּׁאָר מִצְטָרְפִין מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וְעַד שְׁמוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: and the rest combine at four cubits to eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'this תנא' answer of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a version of רבי שמעון that uses four to eight אמות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן יהודה quotes רבי שמעון

steps.title: The twenty-אמות search fits no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from the next part of the source. A twenty-אמות search doesn't match רבי שמעון (twenty-two) or the רבנן (eighteen).
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain it, as רבי שמעון? Then say the next part: 'He checks from there onward twenty אמות.' Whose opinion is this? If it is רבי שמעון, it should be twenty-two! If it is the רבנן, it should be eighteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. Even if the four-to-eight fits רבי שמעון, the twenty-אמות search matches neither opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The search should cover a whole burial cave complex: two chambers with a courtyard between them. By רבי שמעון that is 8 + 6 + 8 = twenty-two, and by the רבנן it is 6 + 6 + 6 = eighteen. So the number twenty doesn't fit either one, and the problem of who wrote the source is back.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you explain it? (literally, 'with what did you establish it?')
Say the next part (the latter clause)
They would be (it should come out to)

steps.confusionAlert: The twenty-two and eighteen come from adding up a full burial cave layout: two chambers plus the courtyard between them. It is not the size of one chamber.

phrases.english: How did you explain it? As Rabbi Shimon?
Then say the latter clause:
He checks from there onward twenty cubits.
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, עֶשְׂרִים וְתַרְתֵּין הָוְיָין!
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Shimon, it would be twenty-two!
phrases.notes: Two chambers of eight plus a courtyard of six between them.

phrases.english: If it is the Rabbis, it would be eighteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתָּא – כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of steps 4–5 using the next clause of the source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the source follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The twenty-אמות search should match a full burial cave complex, which is twenty-two by רבי שמעון and eighteen by the רבנן. So the number twenty fits neither opinion.

steps.title: The source follows the רבנן, measured along a diagonal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the twenty-אמות search really follows the רבנן, in a case where he searched one chamber along its diagonal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the source follows the רבנן, and it is talking about a case where he searched along the diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6 by saying the source follows the רבנן after all. The extra length comes from measuring along a diagonal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the רבנן's measurements, a straight search would only add up to eighteen אמות. A diagonal line across a rectangle is longer than its straight side, so searching along the diagonal stretches the total to twenty. The number in the source now fits the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Diagonal, the slanted line from corner to corner

steps.confusionAlert: Back in step 4 the גמרא said the source follows רבי שמעון. Now, to answer a new question, it switches and says the source follows the רבנן.

phrases.english: Really, it follows the Rabbis,
and it is a case where he searched along the diagonal.
phrases.notes: A diagonal runs corner to corner, so it's longer than a straight side. That's where the extra אמות come from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by placing the source with the רבנן in a specific measuring case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: the search is measured along a diagonal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Twenty אמות doesn't fit the רבנן, whose straight measurement gives eighteen.
steps.terutzMaskana: Measured along one diagonal, the רבנן's layout reaches twenty.

steps.title: Then the second chamber should be diagonal too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if one chamber is measured on the diagonal, the other should be too, which would make twenty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since this one is along the diagonal, that one should also be along the diagonal. Then it would be twenty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. If you measure one chamber on the diagonal, why not the second one as well?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are chambers on both sides of the courtyard. If the diagonal rule adds length on one side, it should add the same on the other side. That would push the total to twenty-two, and the twenty in the source wouldn't fit again.

phrases.english: But since this one is along the diagonal –
that one should also be along the diagonal;
phrases.notes: "That one" means the chamber on the other side of the courtyard.

phrases.english: then it comes out to twenty-two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the diagonal answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a diagonal search makes the total twenty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consistency: if one chamber is measured diagonally, the second should be too, giving twenty-two instead of twenty.

steps.title: Only one chamber is assumed to be diagonal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we assume a diagonal search for one chamber, but not for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say one is along the diagonal; we do not say two are along the diagonal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the diagonal assumption is used for only one chamber. So the total stays twenty, matching the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source can be read as describing one diagonal measurement, which is enough to explain twenty. There is no need to assume a second diagonal on the other side. So the source fits the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: The twenty-אמות search can follow the רבנן: eighteen by straight measuring, plus the extra length from measuring one chamber along its diagonal. A second diagonal is not assumed.

phrases.english: One along the diagonal, we say;
two along the diagonal, we do not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and keeps the answer of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the assumption to one diagonal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both chambers should be measured diagonally, giving twenty-two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one chamber is assumed to be measured diagonally, so the total is twenty.
